en: Hello {person}, we issued {qty} {ppe} on {date}. Please wear it every day for the work it is made for, and tell me when it is worn out.
The machine is {col:machines.age} years old with a planned life of {col:machines.life_years} years. Its value now is {col:machines.value_now}. The age check shows: {col:machines.state}.

In the last 12 months it worked {col:machines.hours_year} hours. Repairs cost {col:machines.repair_year} and fuel cost {col:machines.fuel_cost}. The cost of one hour is {col:machines.cost_hour}. It was down for {col:machines.down_days} days.
The service check shows: {col:machines.svc_state}. Every service is written on the service schedule and signed by the mechanic.
Parts cost {col:repairs.parts_cost}. The workshop worked {col:repairs.labour_h} hours, which costs {col:repairs.labour_cost}. The total cost is {col:repairs.cost}.
The repair was open for {col:repairs.days_open} days and the check shows: {col:repairs.state}. Please keep the invoices for the parts with this statement.
Fuel use report of a machine
Machine: {col:machines.name}. Usual use: {col:machines.fuel_lph} litres per hour.
In the last 12 months the machine used {col:machines.fuel_l} litres of diesel in {col:machines.hours_year} hours. The fuel cost was {col:machines.fuel_cost}.
The diesel price used is the average price paid on your fuel purchases. Every dip of the tank is compared with the stock in the books and a difference of more than {set:fuel_loss} is checked.
A job that uses more than {set:fuel_over} above the usual litres per hour is marked as high fuel use on the sheet Fuel Use per Task.

The contract starts on {col:workers.start_date} and ends on {col:workers.end_date}, which is {col:workers.days} days. The pay is {col:workers.rate_h} per hour. The team leader is {col:workers.leader}.

The worker is paid for the hours on the timesheet. Overtime after {set:ot_day} hours a day is paid at {set:ot_mult} times the normal rate. Picking work may be paid by the kilogram, and the pay is never below {set:min_wage} per hour.
Protective equipment is given free of charge and must be worn. The worker is shown the safety rules on the first day.

Permanent staff pay is {col:payroll.perm_pay}, seasonal workers pay is {col:payroll.seasonal_pay} and piece-rate pay is {col:payroll.piece_pay}. Allowances and bonuses are {col:payroll.allowances}. The total pay is {col:payroll.pay_total}.

Employer costs are {col:payroll.oncost_amt}, so the labour cost of the month is {col:payroll.labour_cost} for {col:payroll.hours} hours. The budget was {col:payroll.budget} and the check shows: {col:payroll.state}.
Please check the timesheets and the piece-rate records before the payments are made.
During the contract the picker delivered {col:workers.piece_kg} kilograms of accepted fruit and vegetables. The piece-rate pay is {col:workers.piece_pay}.
Time work on other days was paid {col:workers.pay}. The total pay is {col:workers.total_pay} for {col:workers.hours} hours.
If the pay for a day is lower than {set:min_wage} per hour, the farm adds the difference. Rejected kilograms are not paid and are shown on the picking records.
The certificate was issued on {col:train.issued} and is valid for {col:train.valid_months} months. It ends on {col:train.expires}, which is in {col:train.days_left} days.
The check shows: {col:train.state}. The next course is planned for {col:train.course_on}. The course cost {col:train.cost}.
A person without a valid certificate must not do the work that needs it, such as spraying, driving a tractor on the road or giving first aid.
Seasonal labour plan for a month

The farm work of the month needs {col:labourneed.hours_needed} hours, which is {col:labourneed.fte} full-time workers. We have {col:labourneed.perm_workers} permanent staff, so we need {col:labourneed.seasonal_needed} seasonal workers.
We have {col:labourneed.seasonal_hired} seasonal workers on contract, so {col:labourneed.gap} workers are still short. The check shows: {col:labourneed.state}.
Hiring must start at least three weeks before the month so that contracts, housing and the safety talk are ready.
What happened: {col:safety.what}. How serious: {col:safety.severity}. Days lost: {col:safety.days_lost}. Cost: {col:safety.cost}.
The action check shows: {col:safety.state}. The record was closed on {col:safety.closed_on}.
Every incident and every near miss is written down the same day. The farm manager finds the cause and writes the action that stops it from happening again.

Open Start and type your farm name and your own limits in the yellow cells: service warning hours, certificate warning days, employer costs, overtime rules, lowest pay and the diesel in the tank when your records start.
List every machine on Machines Register with price, life and day rate. Hired machines only need the day rate.
Add the attachments your tractors pull on Implements, with width and speed, so hectares per hour fill in.
Write every job on Machine Hours Log with machine, attachment, field, task, operator, hours and hectares. Cost per hour of each machine fills in from this log.
Enter the interval and the last service date of each machine on Service Schedule. Hours since the service and the warning fill in by themselves.
Record repairs on Repair Log and breakdowns on Breakdowns and Downtime. Costs and days down update the machine register.
Write every fuel delivery on Fuel Purchases, every job on Fuel Use per Task and every dip of the tank on Fuel Tank Stock to see losses and days of cover.
Keep spare parts on Spare Parts Stock and your contractors on Machinery Hire to compare hiring with owning.
Add your permanent staff on Permanent Staff and their monthly hours and rest days on Overtime and Rest Days.
Register each seasonal or casual worker on Seasonal Workers, then write daily hours on Timesheets and picking kilograms on Piece-rate Records.
Record certificates on Training and Certificates and every incident, near miss and protective equipment issue on Safety Log.
Set your labour budget on Payroll Summary and the hours the farm work needs on Labour Need by Month to see the shortage of workers.

Use the 14 calculators for machine cost, own or hire, fuel, service dates, labour cost, piece-rate pay, pickers, peak labour, overtime, replacement, fuel stock, output, depreciation and seasonal budget.
Read Machinery and Labour Dashboard and Charts every week: services, breakdowns, fuel, labour cost, certificates and safety.
Sell the harvest, milk and eggs at the best net price and get paid
Sell at the best net price, track contracts and get paid on time
Best buyer finder by net price in cash
each quote is cut to a net price after deductions, haulage and days to payment, so the best buyer pays most and not offers most
Net price per tonne after haulage and deductions
each delivery shows the price, the moisture or damage deduction, the haulage and the net price per tonne, set against the market price and your minimum price
Forward contract fulfilment with shortfall penalty
tonnes delivered against tonnes contracted, the weekly pace you still need, the harvest still to come and the penalty you face if it falls short
what each buyer owes split into not yet due and late by 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and over 90 days, with the credit left and a warning at the limit
weight leaving the farm is compared with the weight the buyer reports and every difference above your tolerance is flagged before it turns into a claim
your cost per tonne plus the margin you want gives a minimum price, and every sale and quote is checked against it
days to pay, late invoices, claims and your own view of the buyer give a score from 0 to 100 and a grade that guides the credit limit
Weekly market prices with moving averages
the price you read each week for a crop is compared with the 4 and 13 week averages to show whether the market is rising, falling or steady
Quality claims with days to answer
every claim is linked to the delivery, shows its share of the sale value and warns when it stays open beyond the days you set
fat, protein and cell count place each month of milk in a premium, standard or lower tier and show the bonus or cut in money
storage cost, shrink and interest are set against the price you expect later, with the later price you need to break even
plant health, origin and packing papers for each shipment show who issues them, the days they take and which ones are overdue

Buyers: who buys what, terms and credit
One row for each buyer with country, kind, payment terms and credit limit; sales this year, share, rank, amount owed, credit left and the last sale fill in by themselves.
Sales orders: ordered, delivered and still to deliver
One row for each order with buyer, product, tonnes, price and delivery date; value, tonnes delivered from the sales lines, tonnes left, price against market and a due check fill in.
Sales lines: price, deduction, haulage and net price
One row for each delivery sold with tonnes, price and deduction; net tonnes, value, haulage, net price per tonne, price against market and against your minimum fill in.
Weighbridge tickets: farm weight against buyer weight
One row for each load weighed with truck, driver and times; net weight, the buyer weight, the difference and a weight check fill in.
Forward contracts: tonnes, price and delivery window
One row for each forward contract with buyer, product, tonnes, fixed price and delivery window; value, tonnes delivered, share filled, days left and price against market fill in.
One row for each contract; type the tonnes the harvest can still deliver; tonnes left, weekly pace needed, shortfall, penalty and a status fill in.
Invoices: amount, tax, due date and balance owed
One row for each invoice, made from one delivery; buyer, amount, tax, total, payments received, balance, due date, days late and a status fill in.
One row for each payment with the invoice it settles, amount and method; buyer, invoice total, whether it is a full or part payment and days after the invoice fill in.
Receivables ageing: what each buyer owes and for how long
One row for each buyer; owed now, amounts not yet due and late by 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and over 90 days, credit left and a status fill in from the invoices.
One row for each crop and week with the market price you read; change from last week, 4 and 13 week averages and a trend fill in.
Buyer price quotes compared: the best net price in cash
One row for each quote with offer, expected deduction, haulage and payment days; the net price in cash, rank among the quotes for the same product, market price and a verdict fill in.
Quality claims and deductions raised by buyers
One row for each claim with the delivery, cause, amount claimed and agreed; buyer, product, share of the sale, days open and a status fill in.
Transport and haulage cost for each delivery
One row for each haulage job with distance, rate per tonne-kilometre and fixed charge; tonnes, tonne-kilometres, cost, cost per tonne and a check against your average fill in.
Export documents: certificates and papers for each shipment
One row for each document with the delivery, the type and the dates requested and issued; buyer, country, tonnes, days open and a status fill in.
Farm shop and market day sales
One row for each stall day and product with the kilograms taken, sold and the price; sales, unsold stock and its value, the share sold and a day check fill in.
Livestock sales: auction, abattoir and private sales
One row for each sale with herd, buyer, channel, head, average weight and price per kg live; total weight, value, value per head and a check against your reserve price fill in.
Milk price by quality tier: fat, protein and cell count
One row for each month and herd with litres, fat, protein, cell count and the base price; the quality tier, the price per litre and the value fill in.
One row for each buyer with your own score for ease of work; days to pay, late invoices, claims, sales and a score from 0 to 100 with a grade fill in from the other sheets.
Marketing plan: minimum price and stock per product
One row for each product with expected tonnes, cost per tonne and the margin you want; your minimum price, market price now, sales this year, contract share, stock and stock value fill in.
One row for each disputed or unpaid invoice with reason, amount disputed and recovered; invoice total, amount still at risk, days open and a status fill in.
